content.title: Annual Action Plan for 2026
content.summary: The City of Arvada's Annual Action Plan for 2026 outlines the use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds to address community development needs, focusing on low- and moderate-income individuals. Key objectives include providing essential home repairs for low-income homeowners and supporting public service activities through a human services grant program, with $75,000 allocated for these initiatives. The plan is part of a broader five-year strategy to enhance housing, public services, and economic development in the community.
content.body:
## Executive Summary

### AP-05 Executive Summary – 24 CFR 91.200(c), 91.220(b)

1. **Introduction**  
   The Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) is a flexible federal funding source that the City of Arvada utilizes to address a wide range of unique community development needs. The City prioritizes activities that benefit low- and moderate-income persons. Activities may also be carried out which aid in the prevention or elimination of slums or blight, or certified activities that meet other community development needs having a particular urgency because existing conditions pose a serious and immediate threat to the health or welfare of the community, and where other financial resources are not available to meet such needs. CDBG funds may not be used for activities that do not meet these broad national objectives. The CDBG program ensures that decent, affordable housing is created and preserved, that services to the most vulnerable in the community are implemented, public facilities are sustained, and that economic development opportunities are supported. In accordance with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) entitlement community requirements, City of Arvada prepared a five-year Consolidated Plan in order to implement Federal programs within the community for the period of June 1, 2025, to May 31, 2029. Each year the City of Arvada creates an Annual Action Plan to address the high-priority housing, public service, public facility, and economic development needs of the City, as outlined in City of Arvada’s Consolidated Plan and Comprehensive Plan. The FY26 Annual Action Plan’s program year runs from June 1, 2026, through May 31, 2026.
2. **Summarize the objectives and outcomes identified in the Plan**

   This could be a restatement of items or a table listed elsewhere in the plan or a reference to another location. It may also contain any essential items from the housing and homeless needs assessment, the housing market analysis or the strategic plan.

   The objectives and outcomes in the Plan are the same as those identified in the Consolidated Strategy and Plan Submission for Housing and Community Development Programs City of Arvada, Colorado 2025-2029. Arvada's goals for the 2026 Annual Action Plan period will primarily focus on serving low to moderate income homeowners with essential home repairs as well as assisting low income households through the human services grant program. Services offered through the essential home repairs program will be performed by Brothers Redevelopment to provide necessary improvements to single-family homes owned by low income and elderly residents.

   The City of Arvada will use $75,000 of CDBG funding to support public service activities through the human services grant program.
3. **Evaluation of past performance**

   This is an evaluation of past performance that helped lead the grantee to choose its goals or projects.

   The programs and activities from 2025 were evaluated for past performance from the CAPER and that evaluation shows that the City has made good progress with good performance relative to the Consolidated Strategy and Plan Submission for Housing and Community Development Programs City of Arvada, Colorado 2025-2029.

#### Narrative (optional)

The City of Arvada did consult with local emergency management organizations including Jefferson County Public Health regarding concerns of emergency shelter for people experiencing homelessness. Options for emergency shelter during cold winter months include partnerships with faith-based organizations and other local jurisdictions. The City has completed extensive studies related to water resources in the community to address and plan for future water needs. The City recently implemented a large tap fee and water rate increase to address the growing need for water resources including infrastructure. Additionally the City has been in conversation with the Arvada Fire Department and surrounding jurisdictions regarding wildfire mitigation particularly in the northwest Arvada area. These conversations are a result of the Marshall fire in the Superior/Louisville area. Potential outcomes of these discussions are additional means of egress out of neighborhoods that fall in higher risk areas.

The City of Arvada is also overhauling its internal emergency operation center that will focus on providing critical and lifesaving services during periods of emergency. The essential roles of the emergency operations center include:

Firefighting, public health, mass care, communication, transportation, public safety and security, external affairs, and volunteer donation management. The training and planning involved in these efforts will prepare the Arvada team to continue to provide services for its residents during emergency events such as fire, flood, etc.

The City intends to use CDBG to fund a subrecipient to provide a Single-Family Home Repairs Program. Assistance will also be leveraged through the use of CDBG for collaboration with non profit and other service providers to assist special needs and low/moderate income households with public services as appropriate. In addition to using CDBG, The City will use non-federal funds for gap financing to support affordable housing development and preservation. The city is also utilizing local financial resources for the Safe And Accessible Arvada Program and the Help For Homes Program in partnership with Brothers Redevelopment.

### AP-60 Public Housing – 91.220(h)

#### Introduction

The Arvada Housing Authority (AHA) received an allocation of 562 Housing Choice Vouchers from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The AHA's voucher utilization rate remains extremely high at 98%. The AHA does not own any public housing units.

Foothills Regional Housing (Jefferson County Housing Authority) does own affordable housing developments in Arvada. Foothills and the AHA have maintained a strong relationship over the years and the AHA does its best to support Foothills Regional Housing's affordable housing development efforts.

#### Actions planned during the next year to address the needs to public housing

The AHA does not own any public housing units. To address the affordable housing needs in the community, the AHA will continue its efforts to maximize voucher utilization for its Housing Choice Voucher Program.

The City of Arvada recently completed and adopted the Arvada Housing Strategic Plan that identifies strategies and goals for the City and the Housing Authority to pursue to increase and preserve affordable housing in the community. The newly created Arvada Housing Advisory Committee will develop actionable steps over the next year to achieve these goals.

#### Actions to encourage public housing residents to become more involved in management and participate in homeownership

The Arvada Housing Authority created a Resident Advisory Board to make recommendations to AHA leadership related to the housing authority plan, including policies and procedures. The Resident Advisory Board consists of AHA Housing Choice Voucher participants who wish to provide input and direction.

AHA participants who are interested in homeownership opportunities are referred to the Colorado Housing Assistance Corporation and the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority for education related to downpayment and loan assistance.

#### If the PHA is designated as troubled, describe the manner in which financial assistance will be provided or other assistance

#### Discussion

The City of Arvada and the Arvada Housing Authority have made significant strides over the past two years to increase the amount of affordable housing in the community. The City values its partners in these efforts and strives to include stakeholder input as new policies and partnerships are developed.

### AP-65 Homeless and Other Special Needs Activities – 91.220(i)

#### Introduction

This section discusses the 2026 program year activities that will benefit people who are homeless and populations with special needs.

#### Describe the jurisdictions one-year goals and actions for reducing and ending homelessness including

#### Reaching out to homeless persons (especially unsheltered persons) and assessing their individual needs

The City of Arvada will continue to work to reduce and end homelessness in the following ways:

1. Continue participation in Metro Denver Homeless Initiative Board and committees to help to shape metro wide response to homelessness;
2. Support the creation of permanent supportive housing to serve those who are experiencing chronic homelessness;
3. Fund affordable rental housing developments;
4. Support the continued collaboration of Homeless Navigators/Case Managers within each municipality and Jefferson County (Lakewood, Arvada, Golden, Wheat Ridge, and Jefferson County Human Services)
5. Continue participation in Heading Home and its workgroups;
6. Seek opportunities to increase the housing and support services opportunities of residents who are at risk of becoming homeless;
7. Prevent homelessness by funding programs that provide housing and support services, such as the emergency shelter at Suburban Studios
8. Continue educating community leaders and the public about the needs of residents experiencing extreme poverty and homelessness in Arvada

#### Addressing the emergency shelter and transitional housing needs of homeless persons

The City of Arvada employs two homelessness case managers, one street outreach worker and a housing navigators who collaborate to provide emergency shelter and long term housing resources to the community.

#### Helping homeless persons (especially chronically homeless individuals and families, families with children, veterans and their families, and unaccompanied youth) make the transition to permanent housing and independent living, including shortening the period of time that individuals and families experience homelessness, facilitating access for homeless individuals and families to affordable housing units, and preventing individuals and families who were recently homeless from becoming homeless again

The City of Arvada collaborates with other municipalities and Jefferson County to identify cold weather sheltering options for people experiencing homelessness. This collaboration and planning extends to the federal level including partnerships with FEMA to plan for possible extreme weather situations.  Arvada continues its support of emergency sheltering at a local hotel to provide stability and shelter for households experienicng homelessnes and to connect to resources to provide long term housing opportunities.

#### Helping low-income individuals and families avoid becoming homeless, especially extremely low-income individuals and families and those who are: being discharged from publicly funded institutions and systems of care (such as health care facilities, mental health facilities, foster care and other youth facilities, and corrections programs and institutions); or, receiving assistance from public or private agencies that address housing, health, social services, employment, education, or youth needs.

Through the efforts of the City of Arvada Human Services Advisory Committee, the City of Arvada provides financial support to various non-profit agencies that provide homeless prevention services and other services such as medical, employment and education. The support of these programs will continue in 2026. The Arvada Housing Authority provides permanent housing to extremely low income households throughout the community.

### AP-75 Barriers to affordable housing – 91.220(j)

#### Introduction:

Affordable housing continues to be a priority need in the City of Arvada given the limited supply of rental and ownership units affordable to low and moderate households.

#### Actions it planned to remove or ameliorate the negative effects of public policies that serve as barriers to affordable housing such as land use controls, tax policies affecting land, zoning ordinances, building codes, fees and charges, growth limitations, and policies affecting the return on residential investment

The City of Arvada continues to leverage its existing resources to address affordable housing development barriers. The City's Housing Strategic Plan outlines nine strategies the City will implement in order to address the barriers.

#### Discussion:

AP-85 Other Actions – 91.220(k)

#### Introduction:

This section describes the other actions that the City plans to undertake during the program year to help meet its annual goal and objectives.

#### Actions planned to address obstacles to meeting underserved needs

The primary obstacles to meeting underserved needs in Arvada are limited funding and staff capacity, and barriers to creating affordable housing opportunities (e.g., development barriers and NIMBYism). These obstacles were identified by City staff, relevant stakeholders and community advocates, and by affordable and non-profit developers with housing projects in the area.

To address these obstacles, and to meet underserved needs in the community, the City plans to create a new, dedicated and sustainable revenue source for the Arvada Affordable Housing Fund (AAHF) which was created to support affordable developers and provide gap financing for affordable and attainable projects. (Currently, the AAHF is underfunded for projected needs and does not have a dedicated and sustainable revenue source to help the City meet its housing goals.) The City plans to identify a revenue source through the following action items adopted by the Housing Strategy: consider the feasibility and impact of a small sales or property tax increase; study potential local funding tools and determine the most appropriate source of funds for Arvada; evaluate funding streams for projects in peer cities/communities; and determine concrete priorities for the fund.

#### Actions planned to foster and maintain affordable housing

The City of Arvada adopted the Housing Strategic Plan which includes several short- and long-term strategies and action items to foster and maintain affordable housing. For example, the City plans to invest in the production of income-restricted housing (and to prioritize projects that meet identified housing needs) by setting annual priorities for the allocation of housing project funds.

The City also plans to invest in the preservation of affordable housing (including naturally occurring affordable housing and properties with expiring affordability contracts) by establishing partnerships with local non-profits, housing providers, affordable developers, and other entities who can acquire expiring income-restricted properties and units; work with peer communities to understand existing preservation programs and evaluate the feasibility of similar programs in Arvada; and continue to work across City departments to evaluate how decisions in other areas may impact the affordability of Arvada’s existing housing stock.

Additionally, the City of Arvada will foster and maintain affordable housing through land use and zoning reforms. The Housing Strategy recommends that Arvada update the “affordable” definition to include an affordable for-sale definition, defined by income-restrictions and AMIs rather than LIHTC; consider deeper parking reductions for affordable multi-family projects; consider administrative approvals for affordable developments in mixed-use zones; consider design incentives or alternatives for affordable projects; and/or consider density bonuses for both multi-family and single family affordable projects.

#### Actions planned to reduce lead-based paint hazards

The City will continue to support the Single Family Home Repairs Program which provides critical home repair assistance (including lead-based paint testing and abatement) to low and moderate income homeowners in Arvada. The program is administered in collaboration with Brothers Redevelopment to offer home repair and modification assistance to qualified persons with disabilities, low income individuals and families, and seniors that need crucial home repairs and modifications. As part of the program, homes are tested for lead-based paint hazards and related costs are eligible to be covered by the program.

#### Actions planned to reduce the number of poverty-level families

The City will work to reduce the number of poverty-level families by launching new economic development initiatives and by expanding access to affordable and high quality childcare in the community through the Chamber of Commerce’s BOLD Initiative (among other local and regional planning efforts) and by continuing to allocate funds to Arvada’s Human Services Program which provides financial support to various non-profit agencies that provide critical services to City residents. The City will also work to reduce the number of families in poverty through the Arvada Homeless Navigation Program (AHNP) which is committed to assisting homeless individuals and families in locating permanent housing. Service participation is voluntary and is limited to homeless persons and families that are seeking housing—regardless of other circumstances.

#### Actions planned to develop institutional structure

To implement the goals and strategies outlined in this plan, and in local housing plans, the City of Arvada will monitor staffing needs within the Housing Division and add capacity as needed and will continue to engage with the Housing Advisory Committee (HAC) as a way to establish housing priorities, funding criteria, and goals for affordable housing. The City will also continue to work with the Human Services Advisory Committee to improve the City’s service delivery system to better meet the needs of low income households and special needs populations by providing more targeted recommendations for funding to City staff and City Council members.

#### Actions planned to enhance coordination between public and private housing and social service agencies

To better address housing and service needs in Arvada, the City will work to enhance and improve coordination between public and private housing and social service agencies by working with non-profit and private entities to increase housing and services including but not limited to: Habitat for Humanity, Family Tree, Beyond Home, Brothers Redevelopment, Mission Arvada, The Action Center, and other agencies that may assist the City in increasing affordable and/or supportive housing opportunities for the most vulnerable residents in Arvada. The City will expand on these efforts by looking for opportunities to develop partnerships and/or participate in ongoing partnerships at the local, regional, and state levels.

### AP-90 Program Specific Requirements – 91.220(l)(1,2,4)

#### Introduction:
